differences.what: The label construction itself: triple indicator vectors with <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1 over Q and the dot product over F_2, so triple lines are nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal, in the m-dimensional space F^{(x)3}. B never says what the labels are built from.
Side-wire nesting from t_X perp t_Y, giving <t_X> subset t_Y^perp (paper 945-953 and the 2->5 edge at 1048-1058); A omits the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2, B has nothing on it.

items.note: L3 (only center 3->4 decreases by h, telescoping to Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich) and L5 (100/539, 101/539) are in both (A S5.4.2, S5.4.4-S5.4.6; B K3.A.1-K3.A.3); L1 (residual table) and L4 (orthonormal bases over F_2) are in neither. Only A states the indicator-vector orthogonality that makes the labels nest, plus the L2 inclusion.

Both give rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N negative source projections with first edge 2P_{U_a} of rank one, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0 (A S5.4.7.1-S5.4.7.3, B K3.B.1-K3.B.4), and the endpoint condition giving H<-H+D on every role (A S5.9.2-S5.9.3, B KS.frame). differences.what: Weight is additive mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors, so q_V-q_U = sum_v wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal residual basis.
wt(v) odd gives the phase i^{eps[v.x]}, which H(x)m conjugation turns into the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.
Endpoint repair: the pair X_a->Y_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), turned into C by C=iZC^{-1}Z with sign/phase corrections. B S3.1.e only says corrections give C^{(x)e}.
The kernel count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c < W_c m, deficit 2N-2L_c>0, with no source contribution. B never states s_c's value or that it is below W_c m.

items.note: B has only the proposition's conclusion (product of kernels per residual basis vector, C^{(x)e} after corrections; S3.1.b, S3.1.e). A carries P1, P2 and P4 plus the s_c formula. P3 (k columns) is in neither.

differences.what: The complex case of the saving: deficit 2N-2L_c>0 and s_c/W_c<m^sigma. B derives the deficit only for the bit network (K3.B.4) and states s/W<m^tau generically.

items.note: Both have L/N<1/2 and the bit deficit (R1) and the exponential inequality with log m<20 giving tau=1-2^{-50} (R4: A S5.6.2-S5.6.3, B K3.C). Only A gives the two exact relative deficits and the complex inequality s_c/W_c<m^sigma.

differences.what: B S2.2 says both the controlled shift and multiplication by a fixed unit work by splitting each fibre into two pieces merged in the opposite order. The paper uses two pieces only for the offset; multiplication by c uses c increasing pieces, and negation reverses blocks. A S4's 'blocks re-merged in another order' is accurate.

items.note: Same coverage otherwise (A S3/B S2.1 for the elementary operations). B's method misdescribes the unit-multiplication case, a minor inaccuracy.

Both state A=E_1 Pi E_2 (A S5.7, B K4), M3 linear-cost triangular transformations in descending order (A S5.8.1, B K5.a), the conjugation sequence (A S5.8.2, B K5.b) and M4 one interchange per one of Pi, a in all (A S5.8.3-S5.8.4, B K5.c). Neither gives M1 (the elimination proof) or M2's content. A names a 'fixed odd prime' but not why it avoids the denominators.

differences.what: Child role streams keep a row count divisible by W^{k-1}.
Base case k=0 by the single-digit elementary operation, and the reason the descriptor bound holds (both original chunk ranges remain in every child).

items.note: Both carry the row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi shears per edge implemented by recursive interchanges, the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, the three-update interchange, s calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved to O(e^tau), and the depth-first schedule (A S5.9.x, B KS.*, K10.x). The minor differences balance.

differences.what: Conjugation by the binary address permutation P_M, with M's first columns the residual basis, turns the directional kernels C_{v_j} into coordinate kernels C_{e_j} on slots (eq:phase-edge-coordinate). B has only the directional product (S3.1.b) and never says how directions become slot child calls.
Gaussian elimination writes M in GL(m,F_2) as at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, each an XOR of selected bits across two whole slots, so the non-recursive work is binary row additions.

items.note: Both have the inverse-child identity (A S5.11.3, B S3.1.c), exactly s_c child calls on f=e/m axes (A S5.11.4, B S3.1.d) and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D (A S5.11.4b, B S3.1.f). B lacks the P_M change of basis and its reduction to row additions, the core of the recursion's definition.

differences.what: The family hypotheses (A_rect=O(p), R superpolynomial, f<=d<=p, K/log p->infinity) under which the extra terms of eq:packed-rectangle-time are o(1), and the cost decomposition. B only says 'in the family of parameters used' / 'plus negligible terms'.
Why the packed shifts agree with segment additions off B: guards in [10, 2^{K-1}-11] keep each segment in range under displacement <=8, so no carries or borrows.
The omitted most significant selected position j_{f-1}, supplied at the end by a two-bit XOR.

Neither plan has a step with the eventual-lower-bound or liminf argument (379-387); both only cite n-log-n-conjecture among S0's dependencies.

chain.note: Both follow the paper's route (network with s<Wm, recurrences, transforms, resampling, chirp, CRT, recovery, cost table). A's chain carries the saving for both networks: s_b and s_c each below Wm (S5.4.7, S5.5.3), the exact deficits turning into s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma (S5.6), then the two recurrences (S5.9.6, S5.11.6) feeding the cost table. B's chain thins out on the complex side: it never computes s_c or shows s_c/W_c<m^sigma, which its layer recurrence assumes (S3.3.e). It also lacks the phase mechanism and the P_M change of basis linking edge frames to slot child calls.

errors.says: Adding an offset or multiplying a later field by a fixed unit costs O(V) by splitting each fibre into two pieces and merging them in the opposite order.
errors.paper: Two pieces (split at Q-a) only for the offset; multiplication by c uses c increasing pieces merged by residue, and negation reverses blocks via a stack.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error; B's one slip (the unit-multiplication method in S2.2) is minor. The decisive differences are in the core mechanism: only A gives the phase-interface derivation (weight additivity, odd-weight translation kernels, the 27-coordinate endpoint repair and s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c), the P_M conjugation and row-addition reduction of the phase recursion, and the exact deficits eta_b, eta_c with the complex inequality s_c/W_c<m^sigma. So A's central chain is complete for both networks where B's breaks on the complex side. A is further ahead on the label construction, the guard constants, and several slight items, with no item favouring B.
